status: Narrow production migration complete; six focused shared-build suites passed. Full application integration pending next presentation/layout integration.

sources.behavior: att is a static read-only mount bound through hostPaths.agentAttachmentsDir(deps.agentInstanceId), independent of workspace mounts.
read validates ranges/resolves with read permission and returns a compact loaded-context message. ls resolves with read permission and returns no payload.
att/blob references resolve using the host-owned current agent ID.
Completed tool-read calls retain independent per-call range/preview requests; this extractor does not include tool-ls.

implementation: AttachmentFileBroker::formattedSource returns a value-only FileReadSource closure fixed to the broker agent and accepted physical data/root paths; it captures no QObject.

ToolExecutor routes only formatted read/ls att requests before workspace resolution, copies the closure and existing committer into its cancellable worker, and publishes only the original generation/request result.

Capture pins the attachment directory through the observation. File bodies/mtime are read once through AttachmentStore's existing bounded same-handle reader. Listing uses names from the validated directory handle and refuses directories, reparse entries and invalid flat blob names.
The existing snapshot committer lease, input hash, compact acknowledgment, metadata and pipeline provider reinjection are reused. Original bytes/typed manifests are absent from saved message JSON.
FileReadSnapshotStore explicitly validates att root as a directory and flat att/blob paths as files. Existing clone/remove/revocation preserves the new namespace without new context APIs.

AgentEngine exposes read/ls with an att reader even without workspace/apps, but does not advertise unrelated mutation/command tools in that configuration. Raw sandbox att reads continue through their existing separate broker.

api.FileReadCapture.h: using FileReadSource = std::function<bool(const QString& tool,const QString& path,const FileReadParams&,FileReadCapture*,const std::atomic_bool*,QString*)>;
api.host: AgentToolHost constructor installs the fixed broker reader. No new tool names, result signal arities, session fields or external protocol completion APIs.

evidence.fixtureCoverage: Four-provider ranged reinjection after deletion, typed directory history after clone/deletion, image/binary/ZIP/JAR/WAR/TAR/TGZ rendering, changed fork blob versus cloned original, foreign chat denial, att-only tool availability, traversal/ADS/reserved name/nesting rejection, mutation refusal, unexpected flat entries, canceled reused IDs, lease revocation, snapshot kind/path validation, empty/oversize bytes and Windows root/junction replacement.

limits: This closes formatted access through the existing native flat att namespace; it does not claim unrestricted upstream path equivalence. Native rejects nested blob directories, backslashes and reserved/invalid Windows blob names.

Native formatted captures remain bounded to 4 MiB per file; listing captures at most 4096 flat entries and the existing transformer renders its bounded tree. Archives are listings only, never extraction or execution.

Native ls uses the existing typed manifest+compact acknowledgment lifecycle; pinned upstream ls returns no payload and path-references extracts only read. This is an intentional existing native difference, not newly claimed source parity.

Snapshot eviction remains bounded by existing store policy. Clone/restart guarantees apply while original snapshots remain available; malformed/missing metadata yields existing unavailable-context handling.

Filesystem pinning is strongest on the target Windows implementation. Non-Windows same-handle guarantees are weaker. Concurrent in-place writers can produce a bounded observed byte sequence; this is not a globally atomic filesystem transaction.
Raw Buffer/text att reads stay separate and uncaptured. PDF/Office/RAW/disk/AST transformations and other previously documented unsupported codecs are unchanged.

Explicit tool reads identify the type from the actual blob filename; they do not recover the original friendly name from old attachment-reference metadata. Existing generated imports retain only the final suffix, so a compound .tar.gz import stored as .gz can lose archive inference on later explicit read. This existing filename/catalog gap remains; .tgz and the tested archive extensions are supported.
Fixtures use local generated files and loopback providers only. Six focused production suites passed; full application integration remains pending the presentation/layout integration.
